title: Maguindanao massacre victims' kin urge CA to resolve pending appeals
summary: Families of the Maguindanao massacre victims on Monday renewed their appeal to the Court of Appeals (CA) to resolve pending appeals in the 2009 case, including those involving civil damages and the…

blocks.text: Families of the Maguindanao massacre victims on Monday renewed their appeal to the Court of Appeals (CA) to resolve pending appeals in the 2009 case, including those involving civil damages and the legal recognition of photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay as the 58th victim.
Lawyer Gilbert Andres, executive director of the Center for International Law (CenterLaw) Philippines, filed an 11-page second motion for resolution before the CA on behalf of 19 families.

“Seventeen years na po silang naghihintay, ‘yung iba po ay namatay na po, ‘yung iba po ay naghihintay na sa kanilang mga beds, ‘yung iba po ay may mga sakit na po kaya hindi po sila namin kasama,” Andres told reporters.
(They have been waiting for 17 years. Some have already passed away, others are bedridden, and some are ill, which is why they could not join us today.)
“Kaya sila po ay nagsusumamo at talagang nanghihingi sa ating kagalang-galang na Court office na talagang agaran na po desisyunan lahat po ng pending appeals sa Court of Appeals,” he added.
(That is why they are appealing and earnestly asking the honorable court to immediately decide on all pending appeals before the Court of Appeals.)
The motion was filed on the 17th anniversary of the Nov. 23, 2009 massacre, the deadliest election-related violence in Philippine history.
The attack also remains the deadliest single incident targeting journalists worldwide, with 32 journalists and media workers among the 58 people killed.
The victims’ families also renewed their appeal for Momay to be officially recognized as the 58th victim of the massacre.
The Quezon City Regional Trial Court had acquitted the accused of Momay’s murder and dismissed his family's claim for civil damages.
Momay’s body was never recovered. The only physical evidence linked to him found at the crime scene was a set of dentures.
Earlier on Monday, Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda urged the CA to resolve the pending appeals in the case, saying justice should not be delayed further after 17 years.

“I therefore urge the Court of Appeals to resolve the pending appeals with dispatch, consistent with due process and rights of all parties. Let us ensure that justice is not delayed any further,” Zalameda said.
Andres welcomed the chief justice’s call, saying it reinforced the families’ appeal for the CA to act on the long-pending cases.— MCG, GMA News
